demand.text: Auto is really important, the team says, after some struggles with it the year before; it changed how it makes autos.

auto.text: Four coral from the station: the far back of the reef first, two on the direct line from the source, then the back again. The order cuts driving time, and the back keeps clear of other teams that score on the front.
It dropped PathPlanner for a method it saw OP Robotics use the year before.

cycle.text: Hybrid cycles: a coral waits in the ramp while the robot carries an algae.
An analyst of two 249 point Waterloo matches shows it scoring the algae in the net, then turning to place the coral seconds later, on L4 in one, and also notes a dropped algae and a missed coral.

endgame.text: The reveal thread said there would be no climb at the first event. A deep cage climb was added by the Ontario championship, where it helped secure the barge ranking point in five of six matches on the first day.

fallback.text: Two ramp sensors track the coral, and one that comes in sideways can be unjammed and oriented the right way.
It can pick algae up from the ground.

gave_up.text: Coral comes only from the human player station. A poster who names its funnel as a success says a funnel can slightly lengthen cycles and be easier to defend, but is light.
The first donut climb did not work, and the team said it would start the season without a climb.

changed.text: The elevator went from 5:1 to 3:1 because 5:1 was not fast enough for the four-piece auto.
After Niagara, where coral bounced out of the ramp, a piece was added so it can be fed from farther away.
The deep cage climb came before the Ontario championship.

outcome.text: 46-8-0 in official play; won the OPC - Science division of the Ontario District Championship; did not play in a championship division.
